# MultiversX transaction hash vectors

Generated by `scripts/generate_multiversx_hash_fixtures.cjs` using the official
`@multiversx/sdk-core@16.0.0`. The original vectors use synthetic public signatures. Additional native vectors
come from the production Swift signer with installed WalletCore and the public
BIP39 test mnemonic in `test/native/multiversx_component_harness.swift`. These
prove local serialization/hash agreement, not network acceptance.

Install the exact SDK into a temporary directory with npm `--ignore-scripts`, then
set `NODE_PATH` to that directory's `node_modules` when running the generator.
Redirect stdout to `transaction_hashes.json`. No production dependency is added.

Reference implementation:
- https://github.com/multiversx/mx-sdk-js-core/blob/v16.0.0/src/core/transactionComputer.ts
- https://github.com/multiversx/mx-sdk-js-core/blob/v16.0.0/src/proto/serializer.ts
- https://github.com/multiversx/mx-sdk-js-core/blob/v16.0.0/src/proto/transaction.proto

The Dart codec deliberately handles only ordinary WalletCore transaction fields,
plus the hash-sign option. Guardian, relayer and username fields fail explicitly.
Do not silently ignore new fields when adding support. Hash computation does not
validate the Ed25519 signature or prove that a transaction was submitted.

Regenerate native public transactions with `scripts/test_multiversx_native.py`
and `--fixture-output test/fixtures/multiversx/native_transactions.json` on a
booted simulator, then rerun the SDK hash generator. No private key is exported.
